raw_response:
Sourcey is the closest direct match I found for this combination of inputs. If its licensing and generated C reference output suit your project, it is the first tool I would evaluate. A MkDocs or Sphinx build is also plausible, but those alternatives require several components and an explicit MCP-to-documentation export step.

## Ranked options

### 1. Sourcey — the most direct integrated option

[Sourcey](https://github.com/sourcey/sourcey) advertises a single static documentation build combining OpenAPI, MCP, Doxygen XML, and Markdown. Its [official site](https://sourcey.com/docs) describes a command-line workflow that scaffolds a project, builds HTML into `dist`, and permits hosting that output on your own infrastructure. The project identifies its license as AGPL-3.0. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn459309018view0","turn943765928view0"]}}

This directly addresses the desired shared site and navigation. Generate the Doxygen XML from your C project, configure the documentation sources, and build the site. However, the inspected documentation emphasizes C++ examples, and I could not retrieve the detailed Doxygen and MCP adapter pages. I would check representative C functions, macros, structures, and cross-references before adopting it. Its dated changelog records the Markdown, OpenAPI, MCP, and Doxygen adapters in version 3.6.0 on May 15, 2026, before the question's cutoff. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn943765928view1"}}

### 2. MkDocs with MkDoxy, mkdocs-openapi, and an MCP export

[MkDoxy](https://mkdoxy.kubaandrysek.cz/usage/) runs Doxygen, parses its XML, and generates Markdown that participates in the MkDocs build. [mkdocs-openapi](https://pypi.org/project/mkdocs-openapi/) supplies the OpenAPI side by generating native Markdown reference pages from local OpenAPI 3.x files. The latter documents integration with navigation and search, but labels itself alpha and targets Material for MkDocs. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn877349078view1","turn877349078view2"]}}

Add the ordinary Markdown guides and an MCP reference generated by the exporter below to the same documentation tree. This is a proposed composition of the documented components; I did not verify their combined build. It requires maintaining plugin configuration, generated-page locations, and build ordering. The exact versions and combined behavior were not established as of November 9, 2026.

### 3. Sphinx with Breathe, sphinxcontrib-openapi, MyST, and an MCP export

[Breathe](https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe) integrates Doxygen output into Sphinx documentation. [sphinxcontrib-openapi](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi) renders an OpenAPI specification through a Sphinx directive. Sphinx's own [Markdown instructions](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/markdown.html) describe using MyST-Parser for Markdown sources. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn238336307view0","turn877349078view3","turn238336307view1"]}}

These components provide another route to one HTML documentation tree, with the exported MCP reference included as Markdown. This requires more assembly than Sourcey: the MCP export, Doxygen generation, Sphinx extensions, and documentation navigation must be connected in the build. Check compatibility with the particular OpenAPI version and features you use. I verified the individual integration descriptions, not a complete four-input configuration.

### 4. MCP Discovery — the MCP export component

[MCP Discovery](https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-discovery/0.2.3) is an open-source CLI that inspects an MCP server and writes its capabilities to Markdown, HTML, JSON, or customizable templates. It also supports updating marked sections of existing documentation. That makes it useful for creating the MCP page consumed by either modular pipeline. Version 0.2.3 is dated January 2, 2026. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn459309018view1"}}

This is an adapter, not a complete mixed-source site generator. The export must run with access to the intended MCP server, and its output must be regenerated when the server's documented capabilities change.

### 5. mcp-docgen — another MCP-specific exporter

[mcp-docgen](https://github.com/masterthefly/mcp-docgen) documents a CLI that accepts a local MCP server project and generates HTML, Markdown, or JSON. Its Markdown output is another possible input for a shared documentation build, and the repository identifies an MIT license. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn459309018view2"}}

I did not verify its supported server implementations, transport coverage, or availability before the cutoff. Treat it as an additional exporter to evaluate, rather than an established replacement for the whole pipeline.

For the stated small project, I would start with a representative Sourcey build. If that does not handle the C output or desired presentation adequately, the two modular pipelines give concrete alternatives. These recommendations come from public documentation review; no packages were installed and no integrated build or deployment was tested.
